subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve #96203 by landing fixed managed-service Node heap headroom now, and should that be generated as heap-only `NODE_OPTIONS`, a Node CLI argument, or a tunable install/config surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes managed service startup defaults and crosses the `NODE_OPTIONS` security boundary/resource tradeoff, which requires maintainer product intent before the issue can close.

options.title: Land the narrow fixed default
options.body: Accept #96250's fixed generated heap default now as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require a tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the current fix until maintainers choose a CLI/config/doctor-backed heap-size surface with upgrade proof.

options.title: Use a CLI-argument shape
options.body: Prefer a Node argv heap cap over generated service `NODE_OPTIONS`, folding the #97334 approach into the canonical fix after downstream argv repair proof.

recommendation.title: Land the narrow fixed default
recommendation.body: Accept #96250's fixed generated heap default now as the emergency availability mitigation and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history points to this handle as a daemon service/install surface contributor suited to decide the startup-default tradeoff.
